description: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a quintessential Indian dish known for its vibrant red hue and smoky flavor. Marinated in yogurt and a blend of aromatic spices, the chicken is cooked to perfection over charcoal, resulting in tender, juicy meat with a beautiful char. This iconic recipe brings the authentic taste of a traditional tandoor straight to your backyard grill.

ingredients.notes: hung or thick yogurt for best results

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Make deep slits on the flesh of each chicken piece, especially on the thicker parts, to allow the marinade to penetrate deeply.

instructions.title: First Marination
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with 1 tablespoon of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub this mixture into the chicken pieces, ensuring all slits are coated. Let it rest for 15 minutes at room temperature.

instructions.title: Second Marination
instructions.text: In another bowl, whisk together the plain yogurt, remaining lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, black pepper, and optional food color. Add 1 tablespoon of mustard or vegetable oil to this mixture. Drain any liquid from the first marination, then add the chicken to the yogurt mixture. Coat each piece thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: About 30 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the charcoal to create a medium-hot cooking zone. The coals should be glowing red with a light layer of ash. Lightly oil your grill grates to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Remove the chicken from the marinade, shaking off any excess. Place the chicken pieces directly over the medium-hot coals. Grill for a total of 20-25 minutes, turning every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and charring. Baste the chicken with the remaining mustard oil or vegetable oil periodically to keep it moist and help develop a beautiful crust. Ensure the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with sliced onions, lemon wedges, and a side of mint chutney or raita.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, ensure your yogurt is thick (hung yogurt) to prevent the marinade from becoming watery and to cling better to the chicken.
Kashmiri red chili powder provides a vibrant red color without excessive heat. If unavailable, use a mix of regular red chili powder for heat and a pinch of paprika for color.
Leftover Tandoori Chicken can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in an oven or on a pan to retain moisture.
article:
Unleash the vibrant flavors and tantalizing aromas of India right in your backyard with a classic that never fails to impress: Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This iconic dish, known for its fiery red hue, smoky char, and incredibly tender meat, is a cornerstone of Indian cuisine, celebrated for its robust taste and satisfying texture. While traditionally cooked in a clay tandoor oven, we’ll show you how to achieve that authentic, smoky perfection using your everyday charcoal grill, transforming a simple chicken into an extraordinary culinary experience. Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey that will elevate your dinner table and delight your senses with every succulent bite of homemade Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

At its heart, Tandoori Chicken is a dish originating from the Punjab region of India and Pakistan, where it was traditionally prepared in a cylindrical clay oven called a tandoor. The magic of Tandoori Chicken lies in its unique marinade and the high, dry heat of the tandoor, which cooks the chicken quickly while sealing in juices and creating a beautifully charred exterior. Our focus, Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, aims to replicate this traditional method’s essence by harnessing the intense, radiant heat and distinctive smoky flavor that only charcoal can provide.

The chicken pieces, typically bone-in and skinless, are first incised to allow deep penetration of a rich, spiced yogurt marinade. This marinade is a complex blend of Greek yogurt (or hung curd), ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, and an array of aromatic spices like cumin, coriander, turmeric, garam masala, and most notably, Kashmiri chili powder, which imparts its signature vibrant red color without excessive heat. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, breaking down the chicken fibers, while the spices infuse it with layers of irresistible flavor. When this marinated chicken hits the hot coals of a charcoal grill, the fats render, the spices bloom, and a glorious smoky char develops, making Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled a truly unforgettable dish.

## Ingredients You Need

To create the most authentic and flavorful Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, quality ingredients are key. Here’s a comprehensive list to get you started:

For the Chicken:
*   2 lbs (approx. 1 kg) bone-in, skinless chicken pieces (drumsticks, thighs, or a whole chicken cut into 8-10 pieces)
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice (for the initial marinade)
*   1 teaspoon salt (for the initial marinade)

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup full-fat Greek yogurt (or hung curd, which is yogurt drained of its whey)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   2 tablespoons Kashmiri chili powder (for color and mild heat; substitute with paprika and a pinch of cayenne for a spicier kick)
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed between your palms
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (adjust to taste)
*   1 tablespoon mustard oil (for authentic flavor, or any neutral oil like vegetable/canola oil)
*   Optional: A few drops of red food coloring (for vibrant traditional color)

For Grilling & Serving:
*   Wooden or metal skewers
*   Charcoal and lighter fluid/chimney starter
*   Oil for basting (melted butter or a mix of oil and lemon juice works well)
*   Lemon wedges, sliced red onions, and fresh cilantro for garnish
*   Mint chutney for serving

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Crafting perfect Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a labor of love, but the process is straightforward and incredibly rewarding.

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Wash the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them completely dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits on each piece of chicken. These slits are crucial for the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor and tenderness.
2.  **First Marinade (Optional but Recommended):** In a large bowl, toss the chicken pieces with 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub it well into the slits. Let it sit for 15-20 minutes while you prepare the second marinade. This initial acidic marinade helps tenderize the chicken and enhances flavor absorption.
3.  **Prepare the Second Marinade:** In a separate bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili powder, turmeric powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, crushed fenugreek leaves, black pepper, remaining 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and mustard oil (or neutral oil). If using, add a few drops of red food coloring and mix everything thoroughly until well combined. The marinade should be a thick, vibrant paste.
4.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the chicken pieces to the second marinade, ensuring each piece is fully coated, working the marinade into the slits. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or ideally, overnight (up to 24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness.
5.  **Prepare Your Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before grilling, load your charcoal grill with charcoal and light it. Allow the coals to heat until they are glowing red and covered with a thin layer of grey ash. Spread them evenly for medium-high heat. Clean your grill grates and lightly oil them to prevent sticking. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning.
6.  **Skewer the Chicken:** Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto skewers, making sure not to overcrowd them. Allow a little space between pieces for even cooking.
7.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the skewers directly over the medium-high heat of the charcoal grill. Grill for 15-25 minutes, turning frequently (every 3-4 minutes) to ensure even cooking and charring on all sides. Baste the chicken with a little oil or melted butter during the last 5-7 minutes of grilling to keep it moist and enhance the char. The chicken is done when it's beautifully charred on the outside and cooked through, with an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
8.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and moist chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving restaurant-quality Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled at home requires a few expert tricks:

*   **Choose the Right Chicken:** Bone-in, skinless chicken thighs and drumsticks are preferred for Tandoori chicken as they stay juicy and flavorful. The bone helps conduct heat evenly, and the absence of skin allows for maximum marinade penetration and char.
*   **Don't Skimp on Marinade Time:** The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is truly best for that deep, complex taste.
*   **Use Thick Yogurt:** Full-fat Greek yogurt or hung curd is essential. Regular yogurt is too thin and will make the marinade watery, preventing it from clinging to the chicken. If you only have regular yogurt, strain it through cheesecloth for a few hours to thicken it.
*   **The Power of Slits:** Deep slits on the chicken pieces are non-negotiable. They are the gateway for the marinade to seep in and infuse flavor throughout the meat.
*   **Monitor Grill Temperature:** Start with medium-high heat to cook the chicken through, then move to a slightly cooler part of the grill or raise the grate if you notice excessive charring too quickly. The goal is cooked-through chicken with beautiful char, not burnt raw chicken.
*   **Baste for Moisture and Shine:** Basting with oil or melted butter towards the end of grilling adds moisture, prevents drying, and gives the chicken a lovely sheen and even deeper flavor.
*   **Resting is Key:** Just like any grilled meat, letting the chicken rest for a few minutes after it comes off the grill allows the juices to settle, resulting in a more tender and juicy piece of Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled.

## Serving Suggestions

Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a showstopper on its own, but it truly shines when served with traditional accompaniments. Garnish generously with fresh lemon wedges, which add a burst of acidity that brightens the rich flavors, and freshly chopped cilantro. A side of thinly sliced red onions (laccha pyaaz), often tossed with a little chaat masala and lemon juice, provides a refreshing crunch. Don't forget a cooling mint chutney or raita (yogurt dip) to balance the spices. Serve it alongside warm naan bread, roti, or fluffy basmati rice to soak up all the delicious juices. A simple green salad can also provide a fresh counterpoint to the smoky, savory chicken.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is unbeatable, you can experiment with variations to suit your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Other Proteins:** The same marinade works wonderfully with paneer (Indian cheese), fish fillets (like salmon or cod), shrimp, or even firm vegetables like cauliflower, bell peppers, and mushrooms for a vegetarian Tandoori delight. Adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of Kashmiri chili powder to control the heat. For a spicier version, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or finely chopped green chilies to the marinade. For a milder flavor, increase paprika.
*   **Alternative Cooking Methods:** If a charcoal grill isn’t an option, you can use a gas grill, oven broiler, or even an air fryer. While these won't replicate the charcoal smoke, they will still yield delicious results. For oven broiling, place chicken on a rack over a baking sheet and broil on high, turning frequently, until cooked and charred.
*   **Smoky Flavor Without Charcoal:** If using an oven or gas grill, you can add a smoky flavor by placing a small piece of burning charcoal in a heat-proof bowl within the cooking vessel, drizzling a little oil over it, and quickly covering to infuse the smoke for a few minutes.

Bringing the authentic taste of India to your home kitchen has never been easier or more rewarding. This recipe for Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled promises a dish that is not only incredibly flavorful and tender but also a culinary adventure you'll want to revisit time and again. So fire up your grill, gather your ingredients, and prepare to impress your family and friends with this magnificent Indian dinner recipe. Enjoy the delicious journey!
